question.problem:
Given the vector $x$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{3}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a basis for the solution space of the system. 

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are $2$ pivot columns ($1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. Now, from the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}={x}_{3}$ and from the second equation ${x}_{2}=-3{x}_{3}.$  

So, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{3} \\ -3{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]={x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Consequently, $B=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\}$ is a basis of the solution space of the system.

Finally, we find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{3\cdot 1+(-5)\cdot (-3)+4\cdot 1}{{1}^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{1}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{22}{11}b \\  & =2b \\  & =2[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -6 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
